# **Over Drivin' GT-R (Sega Saturn TNFS) file specs** #

*Last time updated: 2026-11-20 22:23:46.862639+00:00*

*Generated by [TailsLab](../README.md) from its parser code.*


# **Info by file extensions** #

The Japanese Sega Saturn port of TNFS with 8 Nissans in place of the 8 cars, which keep the PC cars' file names (SUPRA = Skyline GT-R PGC10, DIABLO = Skyline GT-R BCNR33, PORSCHE = Fairlady Z 240ZG, VETTE = Skyline GT-R KPGC110, TESTA = Fairlady Z 300ZX, VIPER = Skyline GT-R BNR32, NSX = 180SX Type X, RX7 = Silvia K's). Everything is big-endian (SH-2). The folder `games/tnfs_saturn_gtr` holds the files of the disc (`CDDA/` its CD audio tracks) and the car models sliced from the executable

**0** the executable (loaded at 0x06010000), with the car models, the in-car view records and the car AI records. [TnfsSaturnGtrExecutable](#tnfssaturngtrexecutable). The converter writes the car AI records as PC PDN JSON, `<car>.PDN.json` (and `WARRIOR.PDN.json`)

**CARS/\<car\>.ALL**, **CAR2/\<car\>.ALL** car bundle: physics, the textures of the two models, the cockpit pictures (`CARS` only). `CAR2` is the car's second paint. [TnfsSaturnCarBundle](#tnfssaturncarbundle)

**MODELS/\<car\>/high.orix**, **low.orix** car models, slices of the executable. [TnfsSaturnOrixGeometry](#tnfssaturnorixgeometry)

**SOUNDS/\<bank\>.BIN** engine sounds, Sega sound driver tone banks. [SaturnToneBank](#saturntonebank)

**UIDATA/\<car\>GEN.DAT**, **MEC.DAT**, **PER.DAT** car showcase pages. [TnfsSaturnPcxList](#tnfssaturnpcxlist)

**UIDATA/\<maker\>/MAIN.PCX** car card. A PCX image file (ZSoft Paintbrush; Over Drivin' GT-R: version 5, 8 bits per pixel, run-length encoded, 256-colour palette at the end), kept as its bytes

**UIDATA/FRONTEND.DAT** the menu art: sprite banks, PCX pictures, the palettes, the font. [TnfsSaturnFrontendArt](#tnfssaturnfrontendart). The converter writes `<bank>_<sprite>.png` (banks 0..3, 4 = the font glyphs, 5 = the title screen), `pcx_<index>.png` and `pcx_16_<palette>.png`

**UIDATA/SHOWCASE.DAT** the car showcase pages' sprites (palettes in FRONTEND.DAT). [TnfsSaturnSpriteBanks](#tnfssaturnspritebanks). Exported as `<bank>_<sprite>.png`

**UIDATA/ELOAD/\<car\>/\<n\>.BIN**, **UIDATA/ELOAD/LOAD.BIN**, **UIDATA/ECREDITS/0\<n\>.BIN** race loading pictures and credits pages. [TnfsSaturnRlePicture](#tnfssaturnrlepicture). Exported as `<name>.png`

**HORIZON/\<prefix\>RISE.IM**, **HORZ.IM**, **SET.IM** horizons by time of day, **DASH/HUD\<n\>E.IM** HUD layouts, **DASH/ETICKET.IM** the speeding ticket, **DASH/EMEM2A.IM**, **EMEM2B.IM**, **EMEM2C.IM** backup memory messages: 8-bit pictures after their size. [TnfsSaturnSizedRleImage](#tnfssaturnsizedrleimage). Exported as `<name>.png`

**DASH/EMEM3.DAT** two backup memory messages. [TnfsSaturnSizedRleImageList](#tnfssaturnsizedrleimagelist). Exported as `<index>.png`

**DASH/EMISC.DAT**, **TRACKS/\*.ALL**, the traffic cars **CARS/\<car\>** (no extension), **REPLAY/\***, the other **SOUNDS/\*** and **IP.BIN** are not parsed. **TGQ/\*.TGQ** (movies) are read as EA audio streams (`1SNh`): their sound is exported. **PARAMETERS/\*** copies of the physics at the start of the car bundles (not converted)

Did not find what you need or some given data is wrong? Please submit an
[issue](https://github.com/AndyGura/nfs-resources-converter/issues/new)


# **Block specs** #
## **Physics** ##
### **TnfsSaturnCarPhysics** ###
#### **Size**: 1912 bytes ####
#### **Description**: Player car physics of the Sega Saturn TNFS port (Over Drivin' GT-R): the PC `PlayerCarPhysics` (PBS) layout, 1912 bytes, every 4-byte field big-endian (the grip tables are bytes); the checksum is the PC's (byte sum of the first 1880 bytes), right in every file (checked). The first part of a car bundle `CARS/<car>.ALL` / `CAR2/<car>.ALL` (the two hold the same bytes). Field meanings as in the PC game. The Warrior's physics (not in the car folders) are the PC TRAFFC.PBS byte for byte ####
| Offset | Name | Size (bytes) | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | **mass_front** | 4 | 32-bit real number (big-endian, signed), where last 16 bits is a fractional part | Mass on the front axle (kg). Front weight fraction = `mass_front * inv_mass` (`Fiziks_InitCar`, SE 0x42ff60). Equals `mass_rear` in all files |
| 4 | **mass_rear** | 4 | 32-bit real number (big-endian, signed), where last 16 bits is a fractional part | Mass on the rear axle (kg) |
| 8 | **mass** | 4 | 32-bit real number (big-endian, signed), where last 16 bits is a fractional part | Total car mass (kg), `mass_front + mass_rear`. Only feeds car fields that nothing reads (`Fiziks_InitCar`): the game uses `inv_mass` |
| 12 | **inv_mass_f** | 4 | 32-bit real number (big-endian, signed), where last 16 bits is a fractional part | `1 / mass_front`, rounded down. Only feeds a car field that nothing reads |
| 16 | **inv_mass_r** | 4 | 32-bit real number (big-endian, signed), where last 16 bits is a fractional part | `1 / mass_rear`, rounded down. Only feeds a car field that nothing reads |
| 20 | **inv_mass** | 4 | 32-bit real number (big-endian, signed), where last 16 bits is a fractional part | `1 / mass`, rounded down. Used for the weight distribution, drag / mass (`Fiziks_InitCar`) and the torque table (`tnfs_load_torque_table`, SE 0x409990) |
| 24 | **drive_bias** | 4 | 32-bit real number (big-endian, not signed), where last 16 bits is a fractional part | Front share of the drive force, 0.0 = RWD, 1.0 = FWD (`tnfs_physics_update`, SE 0x430cb0). 0 also enables the burnout rule of `tnfs_engine_thrust` (SE 0x42f138). 0 in all files but LDIABL (0.35) and TRAFFC (0.4) |
| 28 | **brake_bias_f** | 4 | 32-bit real number (big-endian, not signed), where last 16 bits is a fractional part | Front share of the pedal brake force, 0.0-1.0 (`tnfs_physics_update`); the rear gets the rest |
| 32 | **brake_bias_r** | 4 | 32-bit real number (big-endian, not signed), where last 16 bits is a fractional part | Rear share of the brake force, `1 - brake_bias_f` (raw 65536 - `brake_bias_f` in all files). Not read: the game uses total - front |
| 36 | **cog_height** | 4 | 32-bit real number (big-endian, signed), where last 16 bits is a fractional part | Height of the centre of gravity (m). Weight transfer factor = `cog_height * wheel_base_inv` (`Fiziks_InitCar`): moves grip between front and rear under longitudinal force. Rally mode x 1.5 (PSX x 7/4) |
| 40 | **max_brake_force_1** | 4 | 32-bit real number (big-endian, not signed), where last 16 bits is a fractional part | Cap of the absolute longitudinal tire force while braking (brake > 100 or handbrake) below 26.8 m/s (60 mph); also the brake force when the car rolls against the selected gear (`tnfs_physics_update`). Deceleration (m/s²) = this * `force_to_accel` (~10 for ANSX). Rally mode halves it |
| 44 | **max_brake_force_2** | 4 | 32-bit real number (big-endian, not signed), where last 16 bits is a fractional part | Same cap from 26.8 to 40 m/s; above 40 m/s the larger of `max_brake_force_1` and this. Differs from `max_brake_force_1` in 6 of 9 files (ANSX 25.5 / 37.5). Rally mode halves it |
| 48 | **max_tire_coeff** | 4 | 32-bit real number (big-endian, signed), where last 16 bits is a fractional part | Maximal tire coefficient (0.84-1.35). Not read |
| 52 | **drag** | 4 | 32-bit real number (big-endian, signed), where last 16 bits is a fractional part | Air drag (kg/m, ½ * air density * drag coefficient * frontal area). `Fiziks_InitCar` replaces it in memory with `drag * inv_mass`; deceleration = that * surface factor * speed² (`tnfs_drag_force`, SE 0x42f630) |
| 56 | **top_speed** | 4 | 32-bit real number (big-endian, signed), where last 16 bits is a fractional part | Top speed (m/s). Above it `tnfs_physics_update` raises the drag so that it cancels the thrust, except on track id 6 |
| 60 | **efficiency** | 4 | 32-bit real number (big-endian, signed), where last 16 bits is a fractional part | Drivetrain efficiency (0.5-2.0), multiplies the torque table (`tnfs_load_torque_table`); x 0xf8/256 with the automatic gearbox. `Fiziks_PreInitCar` sets it to 0 on a `checksum` mismatch, and when the file `By_R&T` can be created in the CARSPECS folder (DOS flag 0xf7bbe, SE 0x4c5ccc; probably an anti-copy trap, the folder being read-only on the CD). Rally mode: x 0x14c/256 on track 3, else x 0x133/256 |
| 64 | **wheel_base** | 4 | 32-bit real number (big-endian, signed), where last 16 bits is a fractional part | Distance between the front and rear axles (m): car wheelbase and yaw factors |
| 68 | **wheel_base_inv** | 4 | 32-bit real number (big-endian, signed), where last 16 bits is a fractional part | `1 / wheel_base`, rounded down. Weight transfer factor (`Fiziks_InitCar`) |
| 72 | **wheel_track** | 4 | 32-bit real number (big-endian, signed), where last 16 bits is a fractional part | Distance between the left and right wheels (m). Not read |
| 76 | **wheel_track_inv** | 4 | 32-bit real number (big-endian, signed), where last 16 bits is a fractional part | `1 / wheel_track`, rounded down. Not read |
| 80 | **rear_weight_fraction** | 4 | 32-bit real number (big-endian, signed), where last 16 bits is a fractional part | Rear weight fraction, `mass_rear / mass` (0.5 in all files). Not read |
| 84 | **mps_to_rpm** | 4 | 32-bit real number (big-endian, signed), where last 16 bits is a fractional part | Engine rpm = speed (m/s) * this * gear ratio (`tnfs_engine_rev_limiter` SE 0x42ee68, `tnfs_engine_auto_shift_change` SE 0x4098a0, `tnfs_engine_thrust`) |
| 88 | **num_gears** | 4 | 4-bytes unsigned integer (big endian) | Number of used `gear_ratios` entries: reverse, neutral and `num_gears - 2` forward gears. Upshifts stop at gear index `num_gears - 3` (`tnfs_control_shift_gears` SE 0x438c84, `tnfs_engine_auto_shift_change`) |
| 92 | **final_drive** | 4 | 32-bit real number (big-endian, signed), where last 16 bits is a fractional part | Final drive ratio. Only read by `tnfs_load_torque_table` |
| 96 | **wheel_radius** | 4 | 32-bit real number (big-endian, signed), where last 16 bits is a fractional part | Wheel radius (m). Not read, the game uses `inv_wheel_rad` |
| 100 | **inv_wheel_rad** | 4 | 32-bit real number (big-endian, signed), where last 16 bits is a fractional part | `1 / wheel_radius`, rounded down. Only read by `tnfs_load_torque_table` |
| 104 | **gear_ratios** | 32 | Array of `8` items<br/>Item size: 4 bytes<br/>Item type: 32-bit real number (big-endian, signed), where last 16 bits is a fractional part | Gear ratios, index = selected gear + 2: [0] reverse (negative), [1] neutral, [2] first gear and up (`tnfs_engine_rev_limiter`, `tnfs_engine_auto_shift_change`, `tnfs_engine_thrust`). The neutral ratio only gives the wheel rpm in neutral. The first `num_gears` entries are used, the rest is garbage |
| 136 | **num_torques** | 4 | 4-bytes unsigned integer (big endian). Always <= 60 | Number of used `torques` entries (51; 41 in P911), at most 60, the length of `torques`. The game loads that many entries and uses the last one for any higher rpm (`tnfs_load_torque_table`, `tnfs_engine_get_torque`) |
| 140 | **roll_stiff_f** | 4 | 32-bit real number (big-endian, signed), where last 16 bits is a fractional part | Front roll stiffness (10000.0 in all files). Not read |
| 144 | **roll_stiff_r** | 4 | 32-bit real number (big-endian, signed), where last 16 bits is a fractional part | Rear roll stiffness (10000.0 in all files). Not read |
| 148 | **roll_axis_y** | 4 | 32-bit real number (big-endian, signed), where last 16 bits is a fractional part | Roll axis height (m). Not read |
| 152 | **front_roll_stiffness_2** | 4 | 32-bit real number (big-endian, signed), where last 16 bits is a fractional part | 0.5 in all files. Not read |
| 156 | **rear_roll_stiffness_2** | 4 | 32-bit real number (big-endian, signed), where last 16 bits is a fractional part | 0.5 in all files. Not read |
| 160 | **weight_transfer_factor** | 4 | 32-bit real number (big-endian, signed), where last 16 bits is a fractional part | 0.001-0.27. Not read: the weight transfer factor of the game is `cog_height * wheel_base_inv` |
| 164 | **slip_cutoff** | 4 | 4-bytes signed integer (big endian), angle: 0x1000000 means 360 degrees | Max tire slip angle, 24-bit angle: 0x1FE667 = 44.9° in all files. Larger slip angles are clamped to it and set skid bit 1 (`tnfs_tire_forces`, SE 0x42fb88) |
| 168 | **normal_loss** | 4 | 32-bit real number (big-endian, signed), where last 16 bits is a fractional part | Normal coefficient loss. Not read |
| 172 | **max_rpm** | 4 | 4-bytes unsigned integer (big endian) | Engine redline rpm (`rpm_redline` in the game engine). Rpm limit with the throttle = this * throttle / 256 (`tnfs_engine_rev_limiter`, `tnfs_engine_thrust`). Engine sound pitch value = rpm * 127 / (max_rpm + 2000), at most 127 (`tnfs_sfx_engine_player`, SE 0x4444b8, DOS 0x668ab). Tachometer needle: min(rpm, max_rpm + 980) * 600 / max_rpm (SE 0x42221c, 0x420d0c) |
| 176 | **min_rpm** | 4 | 4-bytes unsigned integer (big endian) | Engine idle rpm (`rpm_idle`), engine rpm floor (`tnfs_engine_rev_limiter`) |
| 180 | **torques** | 480 | Array of `60` items<br/>Item size: 8 bytes<br/>Item type: Two 32bit unsigned integers (little-endian): rpm and torque (N*m) | Engine torque by rpm, the first `num_torques` entries are used, the rest is garbage. The game reads only the first rpm and assumes 200 rpm steps (true in all files): entry = (rpm rounded to 200 - rpm[0]) / 200 (`tnfs_engine_get_torque`, SE 0x409a04). `tnfs_load_torque_table` turns each torque in memory into the 16.16 acceleration per unit of gear ratio, `torque * final_drive * efficiency * inv_wheel_rad * inv_mass` |
| 660 | **upshifts** | 28 | Array of `7` items<br/>Item size: 4 bytes<br/>Item type: 4-bytes unsigned integer (big endian) | Automatic gearbox rpm: [g] = upshift from gear index g to g + 1; it shifts down when the rpm in the lower gear would be below 15/16 of [g - 1] (`tnfs_engine_auto_shift_change`). `tnfs_engine_thrust` uses [1] - 500 as the burnout rpm limit. The first `num_gears - 3` entries are used, the rest is garbage |
| 688 | **gear_efficiency** | 32 | Array of `8` items<br/>Item size: 4 bytes<br/>Item type: 32-bit real number (big-endian, signed), where last 8 bits is a fractional part | Per-gear multiplier of the wheel torque, index = selected gear + 2 like `gear_ratios` (`tnfs_engine_thrust`). The first `num_gears` entries are used, the rest is garbage |
| 720 | **inertia_factor** | 4 | 32-bit real number (big-endian, signed), where last 16 bits is a fractional part | 0.5 in all files. Only feeds the car moment of inertia (`Fiziks_InitCar`), which nothing reads |
| 724 | **roll_factor** | 4 | 32-bit real number (big-endian, signed), where last 16 bits is a fractional part | Visual body roll from the lateral acceleration (`tnfs_physics_update`), no unit |
| 728 | **pitch_factor** | 4 | 32-bit real number (big-endian, signed), where last 16 bits is a fractional part | Visual body pitch from the longitudinal acceleration (`tnfs_physics_update`), no unit |
| 732 | **friction_f** | 4 | 32-bit real number (big-endian, signed), where last 16 bits is a fractional part | Front tire friction coefficient: front grip = this * front weight fraction * 9.81 (`Fiziks_InitCar`). Rally mode halves it |
| 736 | **friction_r** | 4 | 32-bit real number (big-endian, signed), where last 16 bits is a fractional part | Rear tire friction coefficient, like `friction_f`. Rally mode halves it |
| 740 | **body_len** | 4 | 32-bit real number (big-endian, signed), where last 16 bits is a fractional part | Body length (m). Copied to the car length, then overwritten by `half_length * 2` of the car PDN in `tnfs_ai_init_car` (SE 0x4407b8): no effect, all 9 cars have PDN sizes |
| 744 | **body_width** | 4 | 32-bit real number (big-endian, signed), where last 16 bits is a fractional part | Body width (m). Overwritten by `half_width * 2` of the car PDN, like `body_len` |
| 748 | **auto_steer** | 4 | 4-bytes signed integer (big endian) | 24-bit angle per m/s (983 in all files). Digital steering, wheel centred, moving forward: the auto-steer target (road heading) is taken only if its absolute value < this * speed (`tnfs_control_steering_a`, SE 0x438954) |
| 752 | **steer_mult** | 4 | 4-bytes unsigned integer (big endian) | Auto-steer ramp multiplier shift (1). Not read |
| 756 | **steer_div** | 4 | 4-bytes unsigned integer (big endian) | Auto-steer ramp divider shift (1). Not read |
| 760 | **steer_model** | 4 | 4-bytes unsigned integer (big endian) | Steering model (2). Not read |
| 764 | **steer_vel** | 16 | Array of `4` items<br/>Item size: 4 bytes<br/>Item type: 4-bytes unsigned integer (big endian) | Auto-steer velocities (2, 4, 8, 16). Only [1] is read: steering rate per tick = min(`steer_vel_ramp` - min(speed * `steer_vel_att`, 1.5), 1.6) * [1] (`tnfs_control_steering_a`) |
| 780 | **steer_vel_ramp** | 4 | 32-bit real number (big-endian, signed), where last 16 bits is a fractional part | Base steering rate (2.2-2.5), see `steer_vel` (`tnfs_control_steering_a`) |
| 784 | **steer_vel_att** | 4 | 32-bit real number (big-endian, signed), where last 16 bits is a fractional part | Steering rate reduction per m/s, at most 1.5 in total (`tnfs_control_steering_a`) |
| 788 | **steer_ramp_mult** | 4 | 4-bytes unsigned integer (big endian) | Shift count: steering rate << this when the target and the auto-steer angle are on the same side of the current angle (`tnfs_control_steering_a`) |
| 792 | **steer_ramp_div** | 4 | 4-bytes unsigned integer (big endian) | Shift count: steering rate >> this otherwise (`tnfs_control_steering_a`; SE and PSX only, DOS has no such branch) |
| 796 | **lat_acc_cutoff** | 4 | 32-bit real number (big-endian, signed), where last 16 bits is a fractional part | Max absolute lateral acceleration (m/s², 17.5-40), also the road grip increment (`tnfs_physics_update`). PSX rally mode x 0.625 |

| 824 | **has_tcs** | 4 | 32-bit real number (big-endian, signed), where last 16 bits is a fractional part | Car has traction control if > 0 (1.0), like `has_abs` |

| 840 | **brake_on_ramp_2** | 4 | 4-bytes unsigned integer (big endian) | Brake rise per tick, x 1.25, from 144 up (`tnfs_control_brake`) |
| 844 | **brake_off_ramp_1** | 4 | 4-bytes unsigned integer (big endian) | Brake fall per tick while the brake is below 144 (`tnfs_control_brake`) |
| 848 | **brake_off_ramp_2** | 4 | 4-bytes unsigned integer (big endian) | Brake fall per tick from 144 up (`tnfs_control_brake`) |

| 860 | **rpm_acc** | 4 | 4-bytes unsigned integer (big endian) | Rpm rise per tick, x throttle / 256, while the gear is disengaged, half in neutral (`tnfs_engine_rev_limiter`) |

| 868 | **drop_rpm_inc** | 4 | 4-bytes unsigned integer (big endian) | In gear: engine rpm rise per tick towards the wheel rpm (`tnfs_engine_rev_limiter`; its branch multiplying this by a per-gear table is unreachable) |
| 872 | **neg_torque** | 4 | 4-bytes unsigned integer (big endian) | Engine braking: force = rpm difference * this / 256 * gear ratio, x 8 when the wheels drive the engine (`tnfs_engine_thrust`) |
| 876 | **incar_camera_height** | 4 | 32-bit real number (big-endian, signed), where last 16 bits is a fractional part | In-car camera height (m, ~1.0) (in-car camera setup, SE 0x405630). Not read by PSX |
| 880 | **center_y** | 4 | 4-bytes unsigned integer (big endian) | In-car view vertical centre (pixels of 320x200): the in-car view windows get the y offset (center_y - 108) * screen height / 200 (in-car camera setup, SE 0x405630). Not read by PSX. The formula is certain, its meaning (projection centre) is an interpretation |
| 884 | **grip_table_f** | 512 | Array of `512` items<br/>Item size: 1 byte<br/>Item type: 1-byte unsigned integer | Front tire grip by slip angle, grip = value / 128 (the game: value << 9 as 16.16). Index = slip angle (24-bit) >> 12: 0.088° steps over 0-45° (`tnfs_tire_slide_table`, read in `tnfs_tire_forces`; DOS 0x593d5). Index 511 is unreachable with the 44.9° `slip_cutoff` and holds garbage |
| 1396 | **grip_table_r** | 512 | Array of `512` items<br/>Item size: 1 byte<br/>Item type: 1-byte unsigned integer | Rear tire grip by slip angle, like `grip_table_f`. Rally mode (DOS, SE) replaces it with the front table in memory |
| 1908 | **checksum** | 4 | 4-bytes unsigned integer (big endian) | Byte sum of the first 1880 bytes (0x758: all but the last 28 bytes of `grip_table_r`). On a mismatch `Fiziks_PreInitCar` sets `efficiency` to 0 |
### **TnfsSaturnCarAiAndCrashBody** ###
#### **Size**: 460 bytes ####
#### **Description**: Car AI and crash body of the Sega Saturn TNFS port (Over Drivin' GT-R): the PC `CarAiAndCrashBody` (PDN) layout, 460 bytes, big-endian, with the top speeds in mph and `gear_count` in 16.16 fixed point. Not a file: 9 records in the executable `0` (`TnfsSaturnGtrExecutable`). The record of the Warrior is the PC TRAFFC.PDN but for those two fields (checked) ####
| Offset | Name | Size (bytes) | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | **half_width** | 4 | 32-bit real number (big-endian, not signed), where last 16 bits is a fractional part | Half width (x) of the collision body (m); car width = 2 * this, it overrides PBS `body_width` (`tnfs_ai_init_car`). Zero in all traffic and cop PDNs: if any of the three half sizes is 0, the sizes come from the car 3D model |
| 4 | **half_height** | 4 | 32-bit real number (big-endian, not signed), where last 16 bits is a fractional part | Half height (y) of the collision body (m), also the collision height offset |
| 8 | **half_length** | 4 | 32-bit real number (big-endian, not signed), where last 16 bits is a fractional part | Half length (z) of the collision body (m); car length = 2 * this, it overrides PBS `body_len` |
| 12 | **moment_of_inertia** | 4 | 32-bit real number (big-endian, signed), where last 16 bits is a fractional part | Crash-body moment of inertia (1.4-2.25), no physical unit; angular acceleration factor = 1 / this (`tnfs_collision_data_reset` and the rebound functions) |
| 16 | **mass** | 4 | 32-bit real number (big-endian, not signed), where last 16 bits is a fractional part | Relative crash-body mass (1.0 typical, 0.5-1.5), no physical unit; linear acceleration factor = 1 / this. Car to car impulses are split by the mass ratio |
| 20 | **handling_factor** | 4 | 4-bytes signed integer (big endian), angle: 0x1000000 means 360 degrees | Racers only (`tnfs_ai_racer_speed`, SE 0x470a9c, DOS 0x80c50, PSX 0x8005bcc8), 24-bit angle (0xA0000 = 14.1°): target speed * (0.8 + 0.203 * (1 - turn / this)), turn = road heading change per track node. 0xFF0000 (TSUPRA, TRAFFC, traffic, cops) = no corner slowdown. Copied to car+0x168, its inverse to car+0x16c |
| 24 | **speed_factor** | 4 | 32-bit real number (big-endian, signed), where last 16 bits is a fractional part | Racers only: target speed multiplier (0.92-1.0) (`tnfs_ai_racer_speed`, car+0x170). 1.0 in traffic and cop PDNs |
| 28 | **power_curve** | 400 | Array of `100` items<br/>Item size: 4 bytes<br/>Item type: 32-bit real number (big-endian, signed), where last 16 bits is a fractional part | AI acceleration by speed (`tnfs_ai_drive_car`, SE 0x46f3e8, DOS 0x7e961, PSX 0x80059d68): speed gain per AI update at index abs(speed in m/s) + 1, x 8 (traffic), x 4 (racers), x 6 (cops), minus the drive argument of the function. The car slows down when [index - 1] is 0. In racer PDNs the first 0 is at the top gear speed rounded up; traffic PDNs have a linear 0.2 -> 0 curve, COPMUST the P911 curve. Uncertain: the exact time scale and the drive argument |
| 428 | **top_speeds** | 24 | Array of `6` items<br/>Item size: 4 bytes<br/>Item type: 32-bit real number (big-endian, signed), where last 16 bits is a fractional part | Top speed (mph, whole numbers in 16.16 fixed point) per AI gear, 0 = gear skipped; the PC PDN holds m/s with its mph factor: PC raw value = mph x 29124 (0.4444 m/s per mph). The Warrior's are the PC TRAFFC.PDN ones (54, 82, 109, 142, 192 mph; checked) |
| 452 | **max_rpm** | 4 | 32-bit real number (big-endian, signed), where last 16 bits is a fractional part | Racers' engine rpm cap, drives the opponent engine sound. 0 in traffic and cop PDNs |
| 456 | **gear_count** | 4 | 32-bit real number (big-endian, signed), where last 16 bits is a fractional part | The PC field (`gear_count`, the traffic horn pitch index) in 16.16 fixed point: 5.0 in every record (PC: the integer 5) |
## **Geometries** ##
### **TnfsSaturnOrixGeometry** ###
#### **Size**: 120..? bytes ####
#### **Description**: Car model of the Sega Saturn TNFS port Over Drivin' GT-R: the PSX ORIX, big-endian (SH-2), version 800, without the CRC footer, with its own polygon and material layouts (`TnfsSaturnOrixPolygon`, `TnfsSaturnOrixMaterial`). The models are not files of the disc: the executable `0` holds them (pointer table at 0x84f14: 9 high-poly models, the 8 cars and the Warrior, 13 zeros, the 9 low-poly ones; car model ids 0..7 = the PC car order SUPRA, DIABLO, PORSCHE, VETTE, TESTA, VIPER, NSX, RX7), sliced to `MODELS/<car>/high.orix` / `low.orix`. Textures: the texture banks of the car's `CARS/<car>.ALL` (`TnfsSaturnCarBundle`). Exported to OBJ + MTL / gg-web-engine GLB as the PC and PSX models ####
| Offset | Name | Size (bytes) | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | **resource_id** | 4 | UTF-8 string. Always == "ORIX" | Resource ID |
| 4 | **block_size** | 4 | 4-bytes unsigned integer (big endian) | Total ORIX block size in bytes, without the CRC footer |
| 8 | **version** | 4 | 4-bytes unsigned integer (big endian). Always == 0x320 | Format version: 800 (0x320), as on PSX |
| 12 | **instance_counter** | 4 | 4-bytes unsigned integer (big endian) | Number of instances of the model at run time (as on PSX). The files have leftovers of a text here (`RAC_`, `NIT\`, `LIS\`, `003\`) |
| 16 | **num_vrtx** | 4 | 4-bytes unsigned integer (big endian) | Number of items in `vertices`: the shape vertices and the morph delta vectors |
| 20 | **num_shape_vrtx** | 4 | 4-bytes unsigned integer (big endian) | Number of shape vertices: `vertices` without the morph delta vectors (`num_vrtx` - the vertices of all morphs) |
| 24 | **vrtx_ptr** | 4 | 4-bytes unsigned integer (big endian) | An offset to vertices |
| 28 | **num_uvs** | 4 | 4-bytes unsigned integer (big endian) | Amount of vertex UV-s (texture coordinates) |
| 32 | **uvs_ptr** | 4 | 4-bytes unsigned integer (big endian) | An offset to vertex_uvs |
| 36 | **num_polygons** | 4 | 4-bytes unsigned integer (big endian) | Amount of polygons |
| 40 | **polygons_ptr** | 4 | 4-bytes unsigned integer (big endian) | An offset to polygons block. Always equals to `120 + num_polygon_textures*8` |
| 44 | **name** | 12 | UTF-8 string | Model name: "_KBNR32B", "_BCNR33W", "_PGC10S"... (high-poly), "_T" + a short name ("_TBCNRW", "_T180SXR") for the low-poly ones |
| 56 | **num_materials** | 4 | 4-bytes unsigned integer (big endian) | Amount of materials |
| 60 | **materials_ptr** | 4 | 4-bytes unsigned integer (big endian) | An offset to materials. Always equals to `uvs_ptr + num_uvs*8` |
| 64 | **num_morphs** | 4 | 4-bytes unsigned integer (big endian) | Amount of morphs |
| 68 | **morphs_ptr** | 4 | 4-bytes unsigned integer (big endian) | An offset to morphs. Always equals to `materials_ptr + num_materials*24` |
| 72 | **num_partitions** | 4 | 4-bytes unsigned integer (big endian) | Amount of partitions |
| 76 | **partitions_ptr** | 4 | 4-bytes unsigned integer (big endian) | An offset to partitions. Always equals to `morphs_ptr + num_morphs*20` |
| 80 | **vmap_ptr** | 4 | 4-bytes unsigned integer (big endian) | Offset of polygon_vertex_map block |
| 84 | **num_fxp** | 4 | 4-bytes unsigned integer (big endian) | Amount of items in fx_polys block |
| 88 | **fxp_ptr** | 4 | 4-bytes unsigned integer (big endian) | Offset of fx_polys block. Always equals to `partitions_ptr + num_partitions*28` |
| 92 | **num_lbl** | 4 | 4-bytes unsigned integer (big endian) | Amount of items in labels block |
| 96 | **lbl_ptr** | 4 | 4-bytes unsigned integer (big endian) | Offset of labels block. Always equals to `fxp_ptr + num_fxp*12` |
| 100 | **num_jld** | 4 | 4-bytes unsigned integer (big endian) | Number of JLD items (verified: when not 0, the game allocates num_jld * 0x24 bytes "INVMATRX" at `jld_runtime_ptr`). 0 in every file |
| 104 | **jld_ptr** | 4 | 4-bytes unsigned integer (big endian) | Offset of the JLD items. Equals to `polygons_ptr` in every file, where there are none |
| 108 | **num_polygon_textures** | 4 | 4-bytes unsigned integer (big endian) | Amount of items in polygon_textures block |
| 112 | **polygon_textures_ptr** | 4 | 4-bytes unsigned integer (big endian). Always == 0x78 | Offset of polygon_textures block (the end of the header) |
| 116 | **jld_runtime_ptr** | 4 | 4-bytes unsigned integer (big endian) | Run time pointer to the JLD inverse matrices (verified), 0 in the files |
| 120 | **polygon_textures** | num_polygon_textures\*8 | Array of `num_polygon_textures` items<br/>Item size: 8 bytes<br/>Item type: Texture of one polygon (verified): the PSX version cuts the texture of a material into one small image per polygon | Textures of single polygons, grouped by material, as in the PSX ORIX: a material with `per_polygon_textures` has `num_polygon_textures` items from `first_polygon_texture` on. The names (`J000`, `J001`...) are textures of the texture bank of the car (`CARS/<car>.ALL`: the first bank for the high-poly model, the second for the low-poly one); polygons of the left and right side share a texture |
| 120 + num_polygon_textures\*8 | **polygons** | num_polygons\*16 | Array of `num_polygons` items<br/>Item type: [TnfsSaturnOrixPolygon](#tnfssaturnorixpolygon) | A block with polygons of the geometry |
| 120 + num_polygon_textures\*8 + num_polygons\*16 | **vertex_uvs** | num_uvs\*8 | Array of `num_uvs` items<br/>Item size: 8 bytes<br/>Item type: Texture coordinates for vertex, where each coordinate is: 4-bytes unsigned integer (little endian). The unit is a pixels amount of assigned texture. So it should be changed when selecting texture with different size | A table of texture coordinates, as in the PSX ORIX. Empty in every file (checked) |
| 120 + num_polygon_textures\*8 + num_polygons\*16 + num_uvs\*8 | **materials** | num_materials\*24 | Array of `num_materials` items<br/>Item type: [TnfsSaturnOrixMaterial](#tnfssaturnorixmaterial) | A table of materials. Items are retrieved by index, located in polygon item |
| 120 + num_polygon_textures\*8 + num_polygons\*16 + num_uvs\*8 + num_materials\*24 | **morphs** | num_morphs\*20 | Array of `num_morphs` items<br/>Item type: [OripMorph](#oripmorph) | Morphs, as in ORIP / ORIX: `left_turn` and `right_turn` (the files hold `left_tur` and `right_tu`; the executable has the strings `left_turn` / `right_turn`, 0x22410) of the high-poly models, each moving 8 vertices: the front wheel steering. None in the low-poly models |
| 120 + num_polygon_textures\*8 + num_polygons\*16 + num_uvs\*8 + num_materials\*24 + num_morphs\*20 | **partitions** | num_partitions\*28 | Array of `num_partitions` items<br/>Item type: [OripPartition](#orippartition) | Partitions, as in ORIP / ORIX: high-poly models have `NON-SORT` (empty), `inside`, `surface` and `outside` (the 4 wheel quads and a few body parts), low-poly models `NON-SORT` with every polygon (checked). The executable has the names `inside`, `surface`, `outside`, `convex` (0x223ac) |
| 120 + num_polygon_textures\*8 + num_polygons\*16 + num_uvs\*8 + num_materials\*24 + num_morphs\*20 + num_partitions\*28 | **fx_polys** | num_fxp\*12 | Array of `num_fxp` items<br/>Item size: 12 bytes<br/>Item type: 12-bytes record, first 8 bytes is null-terminated UTF-8 string, last 4 bytes is an unsigned integer (little-endian). Used by ORIP `fx_polys` (index is a vertex index) and `labels` (index is a polygon index) | Named vertices, as in ORIP / ORIX: the wheel ground points `fl0`..`rr1` (lower case) and the engine point `smok` of the high-poly models (checked; the executable has these names, 0x222fc..0x2231c and 0x22428, and the message "!!! error not Found wheel points") |
| 120 + num_polygon_textures\*8 + num_polygons\*16 + num_uvs\*8 + num_materials\*24 + num_morphs\*20 + num_partitions\*28 + num_fxp\*12 | **labels** | num_lbl\*12 | Array of `num_lbl` items<br/>Item size: 12 bytes<br/>Item type: 12-bytes record, first 8 bytes is null-terminated UTF-8 string, last 4 bytes is an unsigned integer (little-endian). Used by ORIP `fx_polys` (index is a vertex index) and `labels` (index is a polygon index) | Named polygons, as in ORIP / ORIX: the wheel quads `lt_frnt`, `rt_frnt`, `lt_rear`, `rt_rear` (names the executable holds, 0x222dc..0x222f4), the rear lights `bkll` / `bklr` (not in the executable: the game does not look them up) and in some models one part name per body polygon (`Side`, `Topp`, `Undr`, `Circ`, `Shad`, `Frnt`, `Rear`, `Nmbr`, `Pnl1`, `Pnl2`, `Wing`, `Mark`, `Numb`, `Bmpf`; the low-poly models of some cars too). Faults in the files (checked): the PGC10 (`SUPRA`) labels its left front wheel `rt_frnt` too (two `rt_frnt`, no `lt_frnt`); the BCNR33 (`DIABLO`) has a garbage name (bytes e0 01) on polygon 29, `bklr` in the BNR32. The gg-web-engine export names each wheel by its position (see `TnfsSaturnOrixGeometrySerializer`) |
| 120 + num_polygon_textures\*8 + num_polygons\*16 + num_uvs\*8 + num_materials\*24 + num_morphs\*20 + num_partitions\*28 + num_fxp\*12 + num_lbl\*12 | **vertices** | num_vrtx\*12 | One of types:<br/>- Array of `num_vrtx` items<br/>Item size: 12 bytes<br/>Item type: Point in 3D space (x,y,z), where each coordinate is: 32-bit real number (big-endian, signed), where last 7 bits is a fractional part | A table of mesh vertices 3D coordinates: 32:7 points (1/128 m units, the BNR32 is 584 units = 4.56 m long), big-endian. The first `num_shape_vrtx` items are the vertices of the model, the others are the delta vectors of the morphs. X right, Y up, Z forward (the wheel points `fl*` at negative x and positive z) |
| 120 + num_polygon_textures\*8 + num_polygons\*16 + num_uvs\*8 + num_materials\*24 + num_morphs\*20 + num_partitions\*28 + num_fxp\*12 + num_lbl\*12 + num_vrtx\*12 | **vmap** | ? | Array of `?` items<br/>Item size: 4 bytes<br/>Item type: 4-bytes unsigned integer (big endian) | A table of indices the other blocks point into, as in ORIP: vertex and texture coordinate indices of the polygons, the moved vertices of the morphs and the polygon lists of the partitions |
### **OrixPolygonTexture** ###
#### **Size**: 8 bytes ####
#### **Description**: Texture of one polygon (verified): the PSX version cuts the texture of a material into one small image per polygon ####
| Offset | Name | Size (bytes) | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | **polygon_index** | 4 | 4-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Index of the polygon in `polygons` |
| 4 | **file_name** | 4 | UTF-8 string | Name of the image in the PSH archive next to this ORIX (`J000`, `J001`...). Mirrored polygons of the left and right side share an image |
### **TnfsSaturnOrixPolygon** ###
#### **Size**: 16 bytes ####
#### **Description**: A polygon of a Sega Saturn geometry: the PSX ORIX polygon, its first 8 bytes in reverse order (the GPU primitive word first, then the bytes `unk`, `material_index`, `mapping`, `polygon_type`), the offsets big-endian ####
| Offset | Name | Size (bytes) | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | **draw_type** | 4 | 4-bytes unsigned integer (big endian) | The PSX GPU primitive of the polygon (`OrixPolygon.draw_type`): 12 in every file (checked) |
| 4 | **unk** | 1 | 1-byte unsigned integer | Always 0 (checked) |
| 5 | **material_index** | 1 | 1-byte unsigned integer | Index of the polygon's material in `materials` |
| 6 | **mapping** | 1 | 8 flags container<br/><details><summary>flag names (from least to most significant)</summary>0: two_sided<br/>1: flip_normal<br/>2: not_in_draw_list<br/>3: chain<br/>4: use_uv<br/>5: alt_rasterizer</details> | Polygon flags, as in ORIP / ORIX: `two_sided`, `flip_normal`, `use_uv`... Values 0..3 in the files (checked) |
| 7 | **polygon_type** | 1 | 1-byte unsigned integer | Polygon type, as in ORIP / ORIX: bits 0-2 number of vertices, bit 0x08 colour-keyed, bit 0x80 textured. 0x84 and 0x8C (quads) in the files (checked) |
| 8 | **offset_3d** | 4 | 4-bytes unsigned integer (big endian) | Index in `vmap` of the first vertex index of this polygon: the polygon has as many vertices as bits 0-2 of `polygon_type` tell, their indices in `vertices` are the vmap items from this one on |
| 12 | **offset_2d** | 4 | 4-bytes unsigned integer (big endian) | The same as offset_3d for texture coordinates: index in `vmap` of the index in `vertex_uvs` of the first vertex. Garbage when `use_uv` is off |
### **OripVertexUV** ###
#### **Size**: 8 bytes ####
#### **Description**: Texture coordinates for vertex, where each coordinate is: 4-bytes unsigned integer (little endian). The unit is a pixels amount of assigned texture. So it should be changed when selecting texture with different size ####
| Offset | Name | Size (bytes) | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | **u** | 4 | 4-bytes signed integer (little endian) | - |
| 4 | **v** | 4 | 4-bytes signed integer (little endian) | - |
### **TnfsSaturnOrixMaterial** ###
#### **Size**: 24 bytes ####
#### **Description**: A material of a Sega Saturn geometry: the PSX ORIX material, big-endian ####
| Offset | Name | Size (bytes) | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | **name** | 8 | Bytes | Material name, 8 bytes, NUL-padded when shorter: `frntires` and `rertires` (the wheel quads), `tire1`..`tire4` (their textures `Tir1`..`Tir4`, `Tyr1`..`Tyr4` in the PGC10), part names of the body (`side`, `top`, `front`, `rear`, `bottom`, `Circ`, `Shad`, `Topp`, `Wing`, `Numb`...) or empty (low-poly). The executable holds the names `frntires`, `rertires` and `tire1`..`tire4` next to the model loader strings (0x223e4, 0x222c4..0x222d4): the names it looks up |
| 8 | **file_name** | 4 | UTF-8 string | Name of the texture in the texture bank of the car (`CARS/<car>.ALL`: the first bank for the high-poly model, the second for the low-poly one), used when `per_polygon_textures` is off: `Tir1`..`Tir4` for `tire1`..`tire4`. With it on: a part name (`Side`, `Topp`, `Undr`...). Empty in `frntires` / `rertires`: the wheels get a tyre texture at run time |
| 12 | **textures** | 4 | Sub-byte compound block (big endian):<br/>10-bits int "unknown"<br/>10-bits int "num_polygon_textures"<br/>10-bits int "first_polygon_texture"<br/>1-bit flag "per_polygon_textures"<br/>1-bit flag "unknown_bit_0" | Where the textures of the polygons come from, as in the PSX ORIX (big-endian bit field) |
| 16 | **unknown_0x10** | 4 | 4-bytes unsigned integer (big endian) | A colour 0x00RRGGBB per material, different in most materials of a model (grey `Shad`, red `front`, green `rear`, yellow `top`...; 0 in the tyre and the low-poly materials): the colour of the PC ORIP material, it seems. Not known whether the Saturn game reads it (0 in every US PSX ORIX, the Gouraud polygons' colour in the Japanese PSX disc, `color` of the PSX `OrixMaterial`) |
| 20 | **unknown_0x14** | 4 | 4-bytes unsigned integer (big endian) | Values 0..0xF3, mostly different per material (one value per model in the PSX ORIX) |
### **OripMorph** ###
#### **Size**: 20 bytes ####
#### **Description**: A morph (verified): vertices moved by delta vectors times a weight, `vertex = base + round(delta * weight / 0x10000)` per component (weight in 16.16 fixed point, linear) ####
| Offset | Name | Size (bytes) | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | **name** | 8 | UTF-8 string | Morph name, 8 bytes without NUL: the game compares 8 characters of the names it looks up, `left_turn` and `right_turn`, so the files hold `left_tur` and `right_tu` |
| 8 | **num_vertices** | 4 | 4-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Number of moved vertices |
| 12 | **vmap_offset** | 4 | 4-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Index in `vmap` where the indices (in `vertices`) of the moved vertices start |
| 16 | **first_delta** | 4 | 4-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Index in `vertices` of the delta vector of the first moved vertex, the deltas of the others follow it in the order of the vertex indices in vmap. They have the format of vertices and are stored after the `num_shape_vrtx` shape vertices |
### **OripPartition** ###
#### **Size**: 28 bytes ####
#### **Description**: A partition: a named list of polygons, depth-sorted and drawn as a whole. The game draws a car as its `inside`, then `surface`, then `outside` partition (verified), each sorted on its own and painted completely over the previous one: `inside` (the inner tyre faces `circ`, the tyre bottoms `shad`, the Warrior's `bott` and `tire`, some body parts) is always under the body, `outside` (the 4 wheel quads in every full car model) always over it ####
| Offset | Name | Size (bytes) | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | **name** | 8 | UTF-8 string | Partition name. Every ORIP has `NON-SORT`, car models also `inside` and `surface`, full car models and the M*.CFM models `outside`, COPMUST `badge`. The game looks up `inside`, `surface`, `outside` and `convex` (never present); `NON-SORT` and `badge` are never drawn by the car code (verified) |
| 8 | **unknown_0x08** | 4 | 4-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Never read by the game (verified). 0, or a large value equal in all partitions of the model; in traffic and M*.CFM models `inside`'s is the others' + 1 |
| 12 | **unknown_0x0c** | 4 | 4-bytes signed integer (little endian) | Never read by the game (verified). In the full car models 1 for `inside`, 0 for `surface`, -1 for `outside`; 0 in the other models (PICKUP: -1 for `surface`) |
| 16 | **polygons_start** | 4 | 4-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Index in `vmap` where the indices (in `polygons`) of the polygons of the partition start |
| 20 | **num_polygons** | 4 | 4-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Number of polygons in the partition |
| 24 | **unknown_0x18** | 4 | 4-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Never read by the game (verified), always 0 |
### **NamedIndex** ###
#### **Size**: 12 bytes ####
#### **Description**: 12-bytes record, first 8 bytes is null-terminated UTF-8 string, last 4 bytes is an unsigned integer (little-endian). Used by ORIP `fx_polys` (index is a vertex index) and `labels` (index is a polygon index) ####
| Offset | Name | Size (bytes) | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | **name** | 1..? | Null-terminated UTF-8 string. Ends with first occurrence of zero byte | Name of the entry (up to 7 bytes). A few entries have a garbage name, like the bytes 80 02 of a DVIPER `fx_polys` entry (kept as is: a byte which is not UTF-8 is read as U+DC80..U+DCFF) |
| 1..? | **offset** | 7 - len(name) | Array of `7 - len(name)` items<br/>Item size: 1 byte<br/>Item type: 1-byte unsigned integer | - |
| 1 + 7 - len(name)..? | **index** | 4 | 4-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Index of the vertex (`fx_polys`) or polygon (`labels`) |
## **Car bundles** ##
### **TnfsSaturnCarBundle** ###
#### **Size**: 1936..? bytes ####
#### **Description**: Car bundle of the Sega Saturn TNFS port Over Drivin' GT-R: `CARS/<car>.ALL` (the first paint, with the cockpit pictures) and `CAR2/<car>.ALL` (the second paint: the same physics and the same texture names, other colours and pixels, no cockpit). The executable loads `CARS\%s.ALL` / `CAR2\%s.ALL` (strings at 0x22330). The file names are the PC cars' (SUPRA = Skyline GT-R PGC10, DIABLO = Skyline GT-R BCNR33, PORSCHE = Fairlady Z 240ZG, VETTE = Skyline GT-R KPGC110, TESTA = Fairlady Z 300ZX, VIPER = Skyline GT-R BNR32, NSX = 180SX Type X, RX7 = Silvia K's). The car models are in the executable (`TnfsSaturnOrixGeometry`) ####
| Offset | Name | Size (bytes) | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | **physics** | 1912 | [TnfsSaturnCarPhysics](#tnfssaturncarphysics) | Player car physics |
| 1912 | **textures** | 12..? | [TnfsSaturnTextureBank](#tnfssaturntexturebank) | Textures of the high-poly model (`MODELS/<car>/high.orix`) |
| 1924..? | **low_poly_textures** | 12..? | [TnfsSaturnTextureBank](#tnfssaturntexturebank) | Textures of the low-poly model (`MODELS/<car>/low.orix`) |
| 1936..? | **cockpit** | 0..? | Optional (if at least 1 byte remaining): [TnfsSaturnCockpit](#tnfssaturncockpit) | Cockpit view pictures, in `CARS/<car>.ALL` only; loaded for the player of a one-view race only |
### **TnfsSaturnTextureBank** ###
#### **Size**: 12..? bytes ####
#### **Description**: Texture bank of a Saturn car model: 4-bit textures with 16 colours each (VDP1 colour mode 1). Pixels: two per byte, the high nibble first (the left pixel), rows of `width` pixels, top to bottom. Colours: Saturn 16-bit RGB (bits 0-4 red, 5-9 green, 10-14 blue, bit 15 set in every colour), 16 per texture, in texture order. In the high-poly textures of five cars (BNR32, BCNR33, PGC10, KPGC110, 180SX) colour 0 of the rear light texture (the texture of the `bkll` / `bklr` polygons) is pure green, the PSX convention for the brake light colour the game writes at run time; the PSX game takes CLUT entries of pure green (5-bit red < 2, green > 29, blue < 2), the BCNR33's green is 29. Where the Saturn game writes the brake light colours is not known ####
| Offset | Name | Size (bytes) | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | **num_textures** | 4 | 4-bytes unsigned integer (big endian) | Number of textures |
| 4 | **textures** | num_textures\*12 | Array of `num_textures` items<br/>Item type: [TnfsSaturnTextureEntry](#tnfssaturntextureentry) | The textures: high-poly banks have `J000`.. (the polygon textures of the model), the tyres `Tir1`..`Tir4` (`Tyr1`..`Tyr4` in the PGC10) and a few more (`null`); low-poly banks `J000`..`J007` |
| 4 + num_textures\*12 | **pixels_size** | 4 | 4-bytes unsigned integer (big endian) | Length of `pixels` in bytes |
| 8 + num_textures\*12 | **pixels** | pixels_size | Bytes | Pixels of every texture, 4 bits each |
| 8 + num_textures\*12 + pixels_size | **num_colors** | 4 | 4-bytes unsigned integer (big endian) | Number of colours: 16 per texture |
| 12 + num_textures\*12 + pixels_size | **colors** | num_colors\*2 | Array of `num_colors` items<br/>Item size: 2 bytes<br/>Item type: 2-bytes unsigned integer (big endian) | Colour lookup tables, 16 colours per texture, in texture order |
### **TnfsSaturnTextureEntry** ###
#### **Size**: 12 bytes ####
#### **Description**: A texture of a Saturn texture bank: name, size, VDP1 draw mode and where its pixels are. The fields are parts of a VDP1 sprite command (CMDPMOD, CMDSRCA, CMDSIZE) ####
| Offset | Name | Size (bytes) | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | **name_start** | 2 | UTF-8 string | Characters 1 and 2 of the name (`J0` of `J000`) |
| 2 | **width_8** | 2 | 2-bytes unsigned integer (big endian) | Width in pixels / 8 (VDP1 CMDSIZE bits 13-8): widths are multiples of 8 |
| 4 | **height** | 2 | 2-bytes unsigned integer (big endian) | Height in pixels (VDP1 CMDSIZE bits 7-0) |
| 6 | **draw_mode** | 2 | 2-bytes unsigned integer (big endian) | VDP1 draw mode word (CMDPMOD): 0x10C8 or 0x1088 in every texture (checked). Bits 3-5 = 1: colour mode 1, 16 colours from a lookup table (the texture's 16 colours of `colors`); bit 7 (ECD): end codes off; bit 12 (HSS): high speed shrink; bit 6 (SPD): with it (0x10C8) colour index 0 is drawn like any other, without it (0x1088) index 0 is transparent: the wheels, the inner tyre faces, the shadows and the other cut-out textures, whose colour 0 is a key colour (blue, magenta, cyan or black). The export makes index 0 of a 0x1088 texture transparent |
| 8 | **pixel_offset** | 2 | 2-bytes unsigned integer (big endian) | Offset of the texture's pixels in `pixels`, in 8-byte units (VDP1 CMDSRCA): the textures are back to back |
| 10 | **name_end** | 2 | UTF-8 string | Characters 3 and 4 of the name (`00` of `J000`), stored in reverse order: the 4-character name is `name_start` + this (shown in order here) |
### **TnfsSaturnCockpit** ###
#### **Size**: 1040..? bytes ####
#### **Description**: Cockpit view pictures of a car: the dashboard (352x240, colour 0 = the see-through windscreen) and the steering wheel (176x176, colour 0 transparent), each after its size. `Car_Load` 0x06032458 loads them through `Vdp2_LoadRleBitmap` for the player of a one-view race only (`g_split_screen` 0x06082294 = 0). The race screen is 320x224 (every TVMD write is 0x8000): the 3D view shows through the windscreen, the car's cockpit record in the executable (`TnfsSaturnCockpitRecord`) places the needles and the wheel, and the rear view is drawn through a VDP1 user clipping window of 64x23 at the dashboard's (16, 26) at rest, the glass of every car's mirror frame (`Cockpit_DrawMirrorView` 0x0602d1d8) ####
| Offset | Name | Size (bytes) | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | **dashboard_size** | 4 | 4-bytes unsigned integer (big endian) | Length of this field and `dashboard` in bytes |
| 4 | **dashboard** | 516..? | [TnfsSaturnRleImage](#tnfssaturnrleimage) | The dashboard, 352x240: VDP2's NBG0, an 8-bit bitmap in VRAM bank 0 (palette 0). `Cockpit_Update` 0x0601e97c scrolls it by (16 - sway x, -sway y), and the sway's y is -8 at rest: at rest the screen shows the dashboard's (16, 8)..(336, 232), the 16 pixels on each side and 8 rows at the top and bottom are the room the dash sways in. Colour 0 is the see-through windscreen |
| 520..? | **steering_wheel_size** | 4 | 4-bytes unsigned integer (big endian) | Length of this field and `steering_wheel` in bytes: the rest of the file |
| 524..? | **steering_wheel** | 516..? | [TnfsSaturnRleImage](#tnfssaturnrleimage) | The steering wheel, 176x176: VDP2's RBG0 rotation parameter B (the screen's lines from 112 down), VRAM bank 3, palette 1. It turns about its pixel (89, 89) by the front wheels' angle (steer_angle >> 14, 1024ths of a turn), placed by the car's cockpit record (`TnfsSaturnCockpitRecord`). Colour 0 transparent. Its pixels use colours 224..255 and 0 only (checked): RBG0's other picture, the horizon (rotation parameter A, `TnfsSaturnSizedRleImage`), is loaded into the same palette with 224 colours and uses colours 1..223 |
### **TnfsSaturnRleImage** ###
#### **Size**: 516..? bytes ####
#### **Description**: An 8-bit picture: size, a 256-colour palette (Saturn 16-bit RGB) and run-length encoded pixels as in PCX files: a byte from 0xC0 up repeats the next byte (b & 0x3F) times, any other byte is one pixel. Rows of `width` pixels top to bottom, each encoded on its own: no run crosses a row end (checked). 0..3 zero bytes follow the last run: in the cockpit pictures of the car bundles they make the picture and its size field a multiple of 4 bytes (checked), in the `.IM` pictures not always (`HORIZON/AL1RISE.IM` ends with its last run, 45677 bytes). Always after a big-endian u32 size counting itself and the picture. The game loads them with `Vdp2_LoadRleBitmap` 0x0605e83c (bank, palette, colours, x, y, file; `DASH/EMEM3.DAT`'s with its decoding from memory, 0x0605e6f0): it reads the size, then the rest of the picture into memory, decodes it row by row into a 512-byte line buffer (a row ends when it has `width` pixels) and copies the rows to VDP2 VRAM from 0x25e00000 + bank x 0x20000 + x + 512 y, 512 bytes apart; then the colours into colour RAM from colour palette x 256: `colours` of them as they are, or all 256 recomputed per channel when `colours` is negative (0x0605e4b8, not read further) ####
| Offset | Name | Size (bytes) | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | **width** | 2 | 2-bytes unsigned integer (big endian) | Width in pixels |
| 2 | **height** | 2 | 2-bytes unsigned integer (big endian) | Height in pixels |
| 4 | **palette** | 512 | Array of `256` items<br/>Item size: 2 bytes<br/>Item type: 2-bytes unsigned integer (big endian) | Colours (Saturn 16-bit RGB: bits 0-4 red, 5-9 green, 10-14 blue; bit 15 clear in every colour, checked). Colour 0 is see-through in the cockpit pictures (the windscreen of the dashboard, around the steering wheel) |
| 516 | **data** | the size before the picture - 520 | Bytes | Run-length encoded pixels, then 0..3 zero bytes |

#### **Size**: 8..? bytes ####
#### **Description**: Sprite bank of Over Drivin' GT-R's menus: the sprite entries, then the pixels of all of them (8 bits or 4 bits per pixel, rows of `width_8` x 8 pixels top to bottom). Each sprite ends within `pixels`, the last one at its end (checked) ####

### **TnfsSaturnSpriteEntry** ###
#### **Size**: 12 bytes ####
#### **Description**: A sprite of a Saturn sprite bank: size, VDP1 draw mode, where its pixels are and its palette. The loaders (0x060420f4, 0x06042474) keep the entries in a table of sprites, add 1 to the palette (0xFFFF becomes 0) and a VRAM offset to `pixel_offset`; a sprite is drawn with VDP1 colour bank CMDCOLR = the colour RAM slot of its palette (0x06042868) ####
| Offset | Name | Size (bytes) | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | **flags** | 2 | 2-bytes unsigned integer (big endian) | Bit 15 set in every entry; 0x8000 mostly, 0x8100, 0x8200, 0x8A00, 0x9400, 0x9E00, 0xA800, 0xB200, 0xBC00 in a few (the sprites of an animation have increasing values). Unknown, the game ORs more bits into it at load |
| 2 | **width_8** | 2 | 2-bytes unsigned integer (big endian) | Width in pixels / 8 (VDP1 CMDSIZE bits 13-8): widths are multiples of 8 |
| 4 | **height** | 2 | 2-bytes unsigned integer (big endian) | Height in pixels (VDP1 CMDSIZE bits 7-0) |
| 6 | **draw_mode** | 2 | 2-bytes unsigned integer (big endian) | VDP1 draw mode word (CMDPMOD): 0x10A0 (colour mode 4: 256-colour bank, one byte per pixel) or 0x1080 (colour mode 0: 16-colour bank, 4 bits per pixel, the high nibble first) in every sprite (checked); bit 6 (SPD) clear in all: colour index 0 is transparent (the slanted edges of the cards and bars) |
| 8 | **pixel_offset** | 2 | 2-bytes unsigned integer (big endian) | Offset of the sprite's pixels in the bank's `pixels`, in 8-byte units (VDP1 CMDSRCA). Sprites may share pixels with different palettes (the coloured bars) |
| 10 | **palette** | 2 | 2-bytes unsigned integer (big endian) | Palette: palette p of the palette table of `UIDATA/FRONTEND.DAT` (colours p x 256 ..; a 4-bit sprite uses the first 16), at run time p + 1. 0xFFFF = none: the sprite takes the palette of the screen's background picture (colour RAM slot 0): the white title words, tinted with the screen |
### **TnfsSaturnPaletteTable** ###
#### **Size**: 4..? bytes ####
#### **Description**: The palettes of Over Drivin' GT-R's menus: Saturn 16-bit RGB colours (bits 0-4 red, 5-9 green, 10-14 blue), 256 per palette. The loader (0x06042198) reads them into its colour buffer from colour 256 on, so palette p is runtime palette p + 1 (the numbers the sprite loaders make), and copies runtime palettes 1..7 into colour RAM; the others are copied into a free colour RAM slot when drawn (0x06046e20). Colour 0 of most palettes is a key colour (green or magenta), transparent where drawn ####
| Offset | Name | Size (bytes) | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | **num_colors** | 4 | 4-bytes unsigned integer (big endian) | Number of colours: 70416 (275 palettes and 16 colours) |
| 4 | **palettes** | (num_colors/256)\*512 | Array of `num_colors/256` items<br/>Item size: 512 bytes<br/>Item type: Array of `256` items<br/>Item size: 2 bytes<br/>Item type: 2-bytes unsigned integer (big endian) | The palettes, 256 colours each |
| 4 + (num_colors/256)\*512 | **extra_colors** | custom_func\*2 | Array of `custom_func` items<br/>Item size: 2 bytes<br/>Item type: 2-bytes unsigned integer (big endian) | Colours after the last whole palette: the first 16 colours of palette 43 again (16 colours of runtime palette 276, which no sprite names) |
### **TnfsSaturnFontBank** ###
#### **Size**: 8..? bytes ####
#### **Description**: The menu font of Over Drivin' GT-R: glyph entries, then their pixels. 448 glyphs: two fonts (a small one and a big italic one) of 224 characters each, 0x20..0xFF in the Mac OS Roman order (glyph = character - 0x20 + font x 224, the text renderers); missing characters are empty boxes ####
| Offset | Name | Size (bytes) | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | **num_glyphs** | 4 | 4-bytes unsigned integer (big endian) | Number of glyphs |
| 4 | **glyphs** | num_glyphs\*12 | Array of `num_glyphs` items<br/>Item type: [TnfsSaturnFontGlyph](#tnfssaturnfontglyph) | The glyphs |
| 4 + num_glyphs\*12 | **pixels_size** | 4 | 4-bytes unsigned integer (big endian) | Length of `pixels` in bytes |
| 8 + num_glyphs\*12 | **pixels** | pixels_size | Bytes | Pixels of every glyph, 4 bits each |
### **TnfsSaturnFontGlyph** ###
#### **Size**: 12 bytes ####
#### **Description**: A glyph of the menu font: a sprite entry whose width is in pixels. The font loader (0x06041cd4) keeps the width as the advance (one less for most characters), rounds it up to 8 and divides it by 8, rounds the height up to an even number and adds 7 to the palette. The text renderers (0x060428cc, 0x06042aa4, 0x06042d68, 0x06042f88) copy the glyph pixels (4 bits, the high nibble first, nibble 0 not drawn) into an 8-bit VDP2 bitmap as colour base + nibble (0x90, or the caller's base): their colours are those of the bitmap's palette ####
| Offset | Name | Size (bytes) | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | **flags** | 2 | 2-bytes unsigned integer (big endian) | 0x8000, 0x8100, 0x8200 or 0xA800. Unknown |
| 2 | **width** | 2 | 2-bytes unsigned integer (big endian) | Width in pixels; the pixels have rows of this width rounded up to 8 pixels (4 bytes) |
| 4 | **height** | 2 | 2-bytes unsigned integer (big endian) | Height in pixels; the pixels have rows for this height rounded up to an even number |
| 6 | **draw_mode** | 2 | 2-bytes unsigned integer (big endian) | VDP1 draw mode word: 0x1080 (16 colours, 4 bits per pixel) in every glyph |
| 8 | **pixel_offset** | 2 | 2-bytes unsigned integer (big endian) | Offset of the glyph's pixels in the font's `pixels`, in 8-byte units |
| 10 | **palette** | 2 | 2-bytes unsigned integer (big endian) | Palette: 0 in every glyph (7 at run time: palette 6 of the palette table, a green key colour and a grey ramp). Not used by the text renderers |
### **TnfsSaturnRlePicture** ###
#### **Size**: 8..? bytes ####
#### **Description**: A 16-bit picture of Over Drivin' GT-R, word run-length encoded: the race loading pictures `UIDATA/ELOAD/<car>/1..7.BIN` (`WARRIOR/1..3.BIN`; 1 = 3 = 5 = 7 and 2 = 4 = 6 byte for byte), `UIDATA/ELOAD/LOAD.BIN` (0x0604a304) and the credits pages `UIDATA/ECREDITS/01..010.BIN` (0x06063d9c: `0%d.BIN`). Runs: a big-endian signed 16-bit n; n < 0: -n literal colours follow, n >= 0: the next colour n + 2 times. The colours (Saturn 16-bit RGB, bit 15 clear in every one) make rows of 320 pixels top to bottom; every file decodes to exactly `decoded_size` bytes and ends there (checked: 320x224) ####
| Offset | Name | Size (bytes) | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | **magic** | 2 | 2-bytes unsigned integer (big endian). Always == 0x408 | 0x0408 in every file |
| 2 | **unknown** | 2 | 2-bytes unsigned integer (big endian) | 0 in every file |
| 4 | **decoded_size** | 4 | 4-bytes unsigned integer (big endian) | Size of the decoded picture in bytes: 0x23000 = 320 x 224 x 2 in every file |
| 8 | **data** | up to the end of the file | Bytes | The runs |
### **TnfsSaturnSizedRleImage** ###
#### **Size**: 520..? bytes ####
#### **Description**: An 8-bit run-length encoded picture of Over Drivin' GT-R after its size (`TnfsSaturnRleImage`, the layout of the cockpit pictures): the files `HORIZON/*.IM` and `DASH/*.IM` (the size is the file's length, every file decodes completely: checked), the pictures of `DASH/EMEM3.DAT`. Colour 0 is green 0x03E0 in every file. Horizons `HORIZON/<prefix>RISE.IM`, `HORZ.IM`, `SET.IM` (the prefixes of `TRACKS/<prefix>.ALL`: AL1..AL3, CL1..CL3, CY1..CY3, TR1..TR4, and TR5, which has no track file): 512 wide, 78..152 rows, sky and land; RISE mostly with yellow and orange skies, SET red and purple ones; TR4's three files are the same (dark mountains under a night sky), so are TR5's (sand dunes, the sun in a blue sky). `Horizon_Load` 0x060253c0 loads `HORIZON\%sRISE.IM`, `%sHORZ.IM` or `%sSET.IM` (strings 0x06025354, 0x06025368, 0x0602537c) by the time of day byte 0x060fd267: 0 RISE, 1 HORZ, 2 SET, any other value HORZ and the log line "error bad time of day"; `Vdp2_LoadRleBitmap`(2, 1, 224, 0): VRAM bank 2, 224 colours into palette 1. Bank 2 is the race screen's RBG0 rotation parameter A, which draws the screen's lines above 112 (parameter B, bank 3, the steering wheel below, also palette 1: its colours are 224..255). The horizons use colours 1..223 (checked): no pixel has colour 0, which would be see-through (inferred: the two parameters share RBG0's one transparency switch, and the wheel's colour 0 is see-through). HUD `DASH/HUD0E.IM`..`HUD5E.IM`: 352x240, the chase view HUD's six layouts, colour 0 around labels, a rev bar arc of coloured blocks and a dark box: 0 GEAR, TIME, DIST, POS.; 1 LAP for DIST; 2 and 3 RECORD and SPLIT for POS.; 4 and 5 two layouts one over the other (POS., TIME, DIST or LAP, GEAR). `Race_InitCockpit` 0x0601c7f0 loads `DASH\HUD<n>E.IM` (string 0x06081730): 0 / 1 when the int at 0x060c3a4c is not 0, 2 / 3 when it is, 4 / 5 in a split-screen race (`g_split_screen` 0x06082294), the odd one for track numbers (short 0x060fd25a) from 9; it also loads `DASH\EMISC.DAT` (0x06081740, not parsed). `DASH/ETICKET.IM`: 320x224, a police officer holding out a speeding ticket, a patrol car behind (string 0x06080ea0, no direct code reference found). `DASH/EMEM2A.IM`, `2B`, `2C`: 320x224, yellow Japanese text on black: a problem with the console's own RAM (2A), the cartridge RAM (2B), an external device such as a floppy drive (2C): delete (initialise) every save on the save data management screen. Loaded by 0x060406a8 (strings 0x06096f90..0x06096fb0): `Vdp2_LoadRleBitmap`(1, 0, 256, 0, 0, file), the one of the int at 0x060bae94 (0, 1, 2). The E of `HUD<n>E`, `EMEM` and `EMISC` is replaced by the byte at 0x060fd263 before the file is opened. HUD0E, HUD3E and the EMEM pictures store every pixel as a run of one ####
| Offset | Name | Size (bytes) | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | **size** | 4 | 4-bytes unsigned integer (big endian) | Length of this field and `image` in bytes: the file's length for a `.IM` file |
| 4 | **image** | 516..? | [TnfsSaturnRleImage](#tnfssaturnrleimage) | The picture |
### **TnfsSaturnSizedRleImageList** ###
#### **Size**: 0..? bytes ####
#### **Description**: Size-prefixed 8-bit pictures of Over Drivin' GT-R back to back up to the end of the file (`TnfsSaturnSizedRleImage`): `DASH/EMEM3.DAT`, two 320x224 pictures, every pixel a run of one: yellow Japanese text on black, a new save needs 52 free blocks, continue?, with YES and NO, YES highlighted in the first, NO in the second. 0x060406a8 reads both into memory (0x0605e7e8: the size, then the rest) and draws one or the other into VRAM bank 1 (0x0605e6f0, the decoding of `Vdp2_LoadRleBitmap` from memory, 256 colours into palette 0) as the pad moves the choice ####
| Offset | Name | Size (bytes) | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | **images** | up to the end of the file\*520..? | Array of `up to the end of the file` items<br/>Item type: [TnfsSaturnSizedRleImage](#tnfssaturnsizedrleimage) | The pictures |
## **Audio** ##
### **SaturnToneBank** ###
#### **Size**: 8..? bytes ####
#### **Description**: Sega Saturn tone bank (tone data of Sega's sound driver): offsets of the tables, the mixer, velocity, pitch envelope and pitch LFO tables, the voices and the samples. Over Drivin' GT-R `SOUNDS/*.BIN`: the engine sounds of the cars, one voice each. Player banks (`9110` = 911 PORSCHE slot, `DIABLO`, `NSX`, `RX7`, `SUPRA`, `TR512` = TESTA, `VIPER`, `ZR1` = VETTE) have 6 layers: note 50 two looped 8-bit samples, left and right channels of the engine sound (`engine_on`), note 51 the same for the engine without throttle (`engine_off`), note 52 a looped 16-bit sample (the horn, a steady tone), note 53 a 16-bit one-shot (the gear shift: two clunks). Opponent banks `OPP*` have 2: note 40 the player bank's horn at half the sample rate, note 41 the left channel of its `engine_on` at 2^(-9/12) of the sample rate (played 12 and 9 notes lower, so at the pitch of the player's; checked by correlation). Cars sharing a real engine share the engine samples (BNR32 / BCNR33, PGC10 / KPGC110, Silvia / 180SX). The roles are guesses from the data: the game code is not disassembled ####
| Offset | Name | Size (bytes) | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | **mixer_offset** | 2 | 2-bytes unsigned integer (big endian) | Offset of `mixers` |
| 2 | **velocity_offset** | 2 | 2-bytes unsigned integer (big endian) | Offset of `velocity_tables` |
| 4 | **peg_offset** | 2 | 2-bytes unsigned integer (big endian) | Offset of `pitch_envelopes` |
| 6 | **plfo_offset** | 2 | 2-bytes unsigned integer (big endian) | Offset of `pitch_lfos` |
| 8 | **voice_offsets** | ((mixer_offset - 8) / 2)\*2 | Array of `(mixer_offset - 8) / 2` items<br/>Item size: 2 bytes<br/>Item type: 2-bytes unsigned integer (big endian) | Offsets of the voices (one in every file) |
| 8 + ((mixer_offset - 8) / 2)\*2 | **mixers** | 18 \* n | Bytes | Mixer tables, 18 bytes each (effect send levels): one, zeros |
| 8 + ((mixer_offset - 8) / 2)\*2 + 18 \* n | **velocity_tables** | 10 \* n | Bytes | Velocity tables, 10 bytes each: one |
| 8 + ((mixer_offset - 8) / 2)\*2 + 18 \* n + 10 \* n | **pitch_envelopes** | 10 \* n | Bytes | Pitch envelope (PEG) tables, 10 bytes each: one, zeros |
| 8 + ((mixer_offset - 8) / 2)\*2 + 18 \* n + 10 \* n + 10 \* n | **pitch_lfos** | 4 \* n | Bytes | Pitch LFO tables, 4 bytes each: one |
| 8 + ((mixer_offset - 8) / 2)\*2 + 18 \* n + 10 \* n + 10 \* n + 4 \* n | **voices** | custom_func\*4..? | Array of `custom_func` items<br/>Item type: [SaturnToneVoice](#saturntonevoice) | The voices, back to back |
| 8 + ((mixer_offset - 8) / 2)\*2 + 18 \* n + 10 \* n + 10 \* n + 4 \* n + custom_func\*4..? | **wave_data** | up to the end of the file | Bytes | The samples (and a few padding bytes); a layer's `start_address` counts from the start of the bank |
### **SaturnToneVoice** ###
#### **Size**: 4..? bytes ####
#### **Description**: A voice (an instrument): a 4-byte header and its layers ####
| Offset | Name | Size (bytes) | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | **mode** | 1 | Sub-byte compound block:<br/>4-bits int "play_mode"<br/>4-bits int "bend_range" | Play mode and pitch bend range |
| 1 | **portamento** | 1 | 1-byte unsigned integer | Portamento time, 0 in every file |
| 2 | **layers_count** | 1 | 1-byte unsigned integer | Number of layers - 1 |
| 3 | **volume_bias** | 1 | 1-byte signed integer | Volume bias, 0 in every file |
| 4 | **layers** | (layers_count+1)\*32 | Array of `layers_count+1` items<br/>Item type: [SaturnToneLayer](#saturntonelayer) | The layers |
### **SaturnToneLayer** ###
#### **Size**: 32 bytes ####
#### **Description**: A layer of a voice: a note range and the sample it plays. Bytes 2..0x18 are the SCSP slot registers 0x00..0x16 (high byte) the driver writes for it ####
| Offset | Name | Size (bytes) | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | **start_note** | 1 | 1-byte unsigned integer | Lowest note (MIDI number) the layer plays |
| 1 | **end_note** | 1 | 1-byte unsigned integer | Highest note the layer plays |
| 2 | **sample_control** | 2 | Sub-byte compound block (big endian):<br/>3-bits int "unused"<br/>1-bit flag "key_on_execute"<br/>1-bit flag "key_on"<br/>2-bits int "source_bit_control"<br/>2-bits int "sound_source"<br/>2-bits enum:<br/>&nbsp;&nbsp;- 0: no_loop<br/>&nbsp;&nbsp;- 1: normal_loop<br/>&nbsp;&nbsp;- 2: reverse_loop<br/>&nbsp;&nbsp;- 3: alternating_loop<br/>1-bit flag "pcm_8bit"<br/>4-bits int "start_address_high" | SCSP slot register 0x00: sample format and loop mode |
| 4 | **start_address** | 2 | 2-bytes unsigned integer (big endian) | SA bits 0-15: offset of the sample in the bank (the driver adds the address the bank is loaded at): the first sample starts right after the voices (checked) |
| 6 | **loop_start** | 2 | 2-bytes unsigned integer (big endian) | LSA: loop start, in samples from the start of the sample |
| 8 | **loop_end** | 2 | 2-bytes unsigned integer (big endian) | LEA: loop end, in samples from the start of the sample: the SCSP goes back to `loop_start` when it reaches it (without a loop: stops there). The sample data holds `loop_end` + 1 samples (checked: the samples are back to back) |
| 10 | **envelope** | 2 | Sub-byte compound block (big endian):<br/>5-bits int "decay_2_rate"<br/>5-bits int "decay_1_rate"<br/>1-bit flag "hold"<br/>5-bits int "attack_rate" | SCSP slot register 0x08: amplitude envelope rates |
| 12 | **envelope_2** | 2 | Sub-byte compound block (big endian):<br/>1-bits int "unused"<br/>1-bit flag "loop_start_link"<br/>4-bits int "key_rate_scaling"<br/>5-bits int "decay_level"<br/>5-bits int "release_rate" | SCSP slot register 0x0A: envelope levels and release |
| 14 | **total_level** | 2 | Sub-byte compound block (big endian):<br/>6-bits int "unused"<br/>1-bit flag "stack_write_inhibit"<br/>1-bit flag "sound_direct"<br/>8-bits int "level" | SCSP slot register 0x0C |
| 16 | **modulation** | 2 | 2-bytes unsigned integer (big endian) | SCSP slot register 0x0E (MDL, MDXSL, MDYSL): 0 in every layer |
| 18 | **pitch** | 2 | 2-bytes unsigned integer (big endian) | SCSP slot register 0x10 (OCT, FNS): 0 in every layer, the driver sets the pitch from the note played |
| 20 | **lfo** | 2 | 2-bytes unsigned integer (big endian) | SCSP slot register 0x12 (LFO): 0 in every layer |
| 22 | **input_mix** | 2 | 2-bytes unsigned integer (big endian) | SCSP slot register 0x14 (ISEL, IMXL): the effect DSP input and its level (0x0B, 0x07 or 0 in the files) |
| 24 | **direct_level_pan** | 1 | Sub-byte compound block:<br/>3-bits int "direct_level"<br/>5-bits int "direct_pan" | SCSP slot register 0x16 high byte: direct output level and pan |
| 25 | **base_note** | 1 | 1-byte unsigned integer | Note at which the sample plays at 44100 Hz (OCT 0, FNS 0); a note n plays it at 44100 x 2^((n - base note) / 12) Hz. 60 in every layer |
| 26 | **fine_tune** | 1 | 1-byte signed integer | Fine tuning of the base note, 0 in every layer (its unit is not known) |
| 27 | **unknown** | 5 | Bytes | Zeros in every layer |
## **Misc** ##
### **TnfsSaturnGtrExecutable** ###
#### **Size**: 548888..? bytes ####
#### **Description**: The executable `0` of Over Drivin' GT-R (SH-2, big-endian, 598912 bytes, loaded at 0x06010000: a pointer is 0x06010000 + the file offset). Only the car tables are parsed: the cockpit records and the speedometer tops of the in-car view, the car model pointers, the car AI records and their pointers. Also in it: the car models themselves (ORIX, `TnfsSaturnOrixGeometry`), the short car names at 0x47df0 (`SILVIA`, `180SX`, `BNR32`, `300ZX`, `KPGC110`, `240ZG`, `BCNR33`, `PGC10`) and the names the model loader looks up (0x222c4..0x2242c) ####
| Offset | Name | Size (bytes) | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | **code** | 464304 | Bytes | Code and data before the cockpit records |
| 464304 | **cockpit_records** | 288 | Array of `9` items<br/>Item type: [TnfsSaturnCockpitRecord](#tnfssaturncockpitrecord) | The in-car view records by car model id (`g_cockpit_table` 0x060815b0): 0 SUPRA (PGC10), 1 DIABLO (BCNR33), 2 PORSCHE (240ZG), 3 VETTE (KPGC110), 4 TESTA (300ZX), 5 VIPER (BNR32), 6 NSX (180SX), 7 RX7 (Silvia), 8 the Warrior. Read by `Race_InitCockpit` 0x0601c7f0 and `Cockpit_DrawNeedles` 0x0601e7a4 |
| 464592 | **code_after_cockpit_records** | 404 | Bytes | Code and data between the cockpit records and the speedometer tops |
| 464996 | **speedometer_tops** | 32 | Array of `8` items<br/>Item size: 4 bytes<br/>Item type: 4-bytes signed integer (big endian) | The speedometer's top by car model id 0..7 (`g_speedo_clamp` 0x06081864): 240 for 0 and 3 (PGC10, KPGC110), 180 for the others. Read by `Cockpit_DrawNeedles` 0x0601e7a4, which clamps the speed and the car's top speed to it (both in the display unit, km/h or mph) before the needle angle; it draws no speedometer for model 8 (the Warrior) |
| 465028 | **code_after_speedometer_tops** | 79504 | Bytes | Code and data between the speedometer tops and the car model pointers |
| 544532 | **model_pointers** | 124 | Array of `31` items<br/>Item size: 4 bytes<br/>Item type: 4-bytes unsigned integer (big endian) | Car model pointers: [0..8] the high-poly models of car model ids 0..7 (SUPRA, DIABLO, PORSCHE, VETTE, TESTA, VIPER, NSX, RX7) and of the Warrior, [9..21] 0, [22..30] the low-poly models in the same order |
| 544656 | **car_ai_records** | 4140 | Array of `9` items<br/>Item type: [TnfsSaturnCarAiAndCrashBody](#tnfssaturncaraiandcrashbody) | Car AI records (PC PDN), 9 of them: [0] the Warrior, [1] NSX, [2] PORSCHE, [3] TESTA, [4] DIABLO, [5] VIPER, [6] VETTE, [7] SUPRA, [8] RX7 (by `car_ai_pointers`) |
| 548796 | **car_ai_pointers** | 92 | Array of `23` items<br/>Item size: 4 bytes<br/>Item type: 4-bytes unsigned integer (big endian) | Pointers to `car_ai_records`: [13 + car model id] the record of each car (model ids 0..7 -> records 7, 4, 2, 6, 3, 5, 1, 8), [21] and [22] the Warrior's (record 0), [0..12] record 7 (SUPRA) |
| 548888 | **rest** | up to the end of the file | Bytes | Code and data after the car AI pointers |
### **TnfsSaturnCockpitRecord** ###
#### **Size**: 32 bytes ####
#### **Description**: A car model's in-car view record of Over Drivin' GT-R's executable (`g_cockpit_table` 0x060815b0, 0x20 bytes, big-endian, signed 16-bit unless said): the needles drawn over the dashboard and where the steering wheel goes, in screen pixels of the 320x224 race screen. `Race_InitCockpit` 0x0601c7f0 takes the record of the player's car model and sets the needle colour and the wheel's rotation parameters; `Cockpit_Update` 0x0601e97c adds the dash's sway every frame and `Cockpit_DrawNeedles` 0x0601e7a4 draws the needles as VDP1 lines: the angle a (`math_div`), its sine and cosine (1024-entry 16.16 tables at 0x0607fa60 / 0x0607fe60), each product with a length >> 16; down-left at a = 0, clockwise as a grows. The sway is (0, -8) at rest, so a centre (x, y) is the dashboard picture's (x + 16, y). The Warrior's record (model 8) has tachometer lengths 29, 11 and no speedometer (all 0: a digital speedometer) ####
| Offset | Name | Size (bytes) | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | **needle_color** | 2 | 2-bytes unsigned integer (big endian) | Needle colour (Saturn 16-bit RGB): `Race_InitCockpit` puts it into colour RAM colour 0x7f0, the needles are VDP1 lines of colour code 0x27f0. 0x0016 (red) but model 0 (0x2d6b, grey) and models 2 and 3 (0x5ad6, light grey) |
| 2 | **tachometer_x_length** | 1 | 1-byte unsigned integer | Length L1 of the tachometer needle's x part (the high byte of a big-endian short): the needle goes from the centre to centre + (-(L1 sin a + L1 cos a), L2 cos a - L2 sin a) |
| 3 | **tachometer_y_length** | 1 | 1-byte unsigned integer | Length L2 of the tachometer needle's y part (the low byte) |
| 4 | **tachometer_x** | 2 | 2-bytes signed integer (big endian) | The tachometer's centre x on the screen, + the sway's x: at rest the dashboard's x + 16 |
| 6 | **tachometer_y** | 2 | 2-bytes signed integer (big endian) | The tachometer's centre y on the screen, + the sway's y (-8 at rest): at rest the dashboard's y |
| 8 | **tachometer_scale** | 2 | 2-bytes signed integer (big endian) | Needle angle a = rpm x scale / max rpm + offset, in 1024ths of a turn (max rpm: the PBS one, the rpm clamped to it) |
| 10 | **tachometer_offset** | 2 | 2-bytes signed integer (big endian) | Added to the needle angle, 1024ths of a turn; can be negative (-174 in model 1) |
| 12 | **speedometer_x_length** | 1 | 1-byte unsigned integer | Length L1 of the speedometer needle's x part (the high byte of a big-endian short): the needle goes from the centre to centre + (-(L1 sin a + L1 cos a), L2 cos a - L2 sin a) |
| 13 | **speedometer_y_length** | 1 | 1-byte unsigned integer | Length L2 of the speedometer needle's y part (the low byte) |
| 14 | **speedometer_x** | 2 | 2-bytes signed integer (big endian) | The speedometer's centre x on the screen, + the sway's x: at rest the dashboard's x + 16 |
| 16 | **speedometer_y** | 2 | 2-bytes signed integer (big endian) | The speedometer's centre y on the screen, + the sway's y (-8 at rest): at rest the dashboard's y |
| 18 | **speedometer_scale** | 2 | 2-bytes signed integer (big endian) | Needle angle a = min(speed, top) x scale / min(the car's top speed, top) + offset, in 1024ths of a turn (the speeds in the display unit, km/h or mph; top: the model's entry of the executable's `speedometer_tops`) |
| 20 | **speedometer_offset** | 2 | 2-bytes signed integer (big endian) | Added to the needle angle, 1024ths of a turn; can be negative (-38 in model 5) |
| 22 | **steering_wheel_left** | 2 | 2-bytes signed integer (big endian) | Where the steering wheel picture goes: rotation parameter B's Xst = -(left + sway x / 2) << 16, its left edge at screen x left + sway x / 2, at rest the dashboard's x left + 16. 72 but model 3 (74) |
| 24 | **steering_wheel_top** | 2 | 2-bytes signed integer (big endian) | Yst = -(top + sway y) << 16: the wheel picture's top edge at screen y top + sway y, at rest the dashboard's y top. 128 but model 6 (136) |
| 26 | **steering_wheel_pivot_x** | 2 | 2-bytes signed integer (big endian) | The wheel's rotation centre x in its picture (rotation parameter B's Px and Cx): 89 in every record |
| 28 | **steering_wheel_pivot_y** | 2 | 2-bytes signed integer (big endian) | The rotation centre y (Py and Cy): 89 in every record |
| 30 | **unknown** | 2 | 2-bytes unsigned integer (big endian) | 0 in every record |
